best_for: Developers who query Postgres, MySQL, SQLite or SQL Server most days and want a clean desktop SQL editor for free, with paid tiers only if they need Oracle, MongoDB or data import tools.
description:
Beekeeper Studio is a SQL editor and database manager from the Beekeeper Studio team. It aims to feel like a spreadsheet, with Excel-style keys for moving around and editing data, and since version 6.2 you can add plugins from a built-in store.

A fuzzy quick search jumps to any table, and foreign keys show up as links you can click to see the related row. The JSON sidebar lays out a record from top to bottom, and long values open full screen. When you change data, the edits are staged for review first, and you can copy them out as SQL instead of running them. Color-coded connections and a read-only switch help you tell production from test.

points.title: Free edition covers the common databases
points.text: The GPLv3 Community edition connects to PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, SQL Server, Redshift, CockroachDB, BigQuery and Redis, among others. For day-to-day querying and browsing tables, many people never need more.

points.title: Where the free edition stops
points.text: Community leaves out editing query results in place, import and export, backup and restore, the AI shell, cloud workspaces and more than 2 filters per table. Oracle, Cassandra, DuckDB, ClickHouse, MongoDB, Snowflake and several others need a paid plan.

points.title: Paid plans, billed yearly
points.text: Indie is USD 9 per user per month billed yearly, for 1 device per user. Professional is USD 14 and Business USD 18, both with unlimited devices; Business adds Snowflake and Kerberos, IAM and Entra ID sign-in. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: You keep what you paid for
points.text: Yearly subscribers get a lifetime license to every version released while they paid; monthly subscribers earn it after 12 months in a row. Cloud workspaces still need an active plan. When a trial ends, the app drops back to Community and keeps your saved connections.

points.title: One download for every edition
points.text: There is a single app, and you turn on paid features from inside it. You do not need to reinstall to upgrade or downgrade.

points.title: Linux build here is behind
points.text: The Flatpak listed here is at 5.8.1 while Windows and macOS are at 6.3.3, and Flathub does not mark it as verified. If you want the current release on Linux, check the downloads on beekeeperstudio.io.

points.title: A long version trail on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 132 versions, with x64 and Arm64 installers for one user or the whole machine. macOS has Intel and Apple Silicon builds for macOS 13 or later, but lists only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
